gloss: Bashō (the haiku poet); Japanese banana plant

definitions.explanation: The usual way of referring to Matsuo Bashō (1644–1694), the most famous haiku poet. His pen name comes from a banana plant (sense 2) growing beside his hut in Edo.
A large plant of the banana family with broad, tearing leaves, grown in gardens for its leaves; its fruit is not eaten.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 1 is by far the more common: Japanese refers to the poet by his pen name alone, as English does with "Bashō". The full name has its own entry, ⟦{松尾芭蕉|まつおばしょう}→松尾芭蕉：30772_matsuobashou⟧.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {芭蕉|ばしょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{句|く}→句：02137_ku⟧: a haiku by Bashō
- {古池|ふるいけ}や{蛙|かわず}⟦{飛|と}び{込|こ}む→飛び込む：04614_tobikomu⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{音|おと}→音：00743_oto⟧: "An old pond / a frog jumps in / the sound of water", his best-known verse
